headings.title: Short title of act
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2025 S.B. 348 § 226.804). Designates this section as the 'Route 66 Signage Maintenance and Enhancement Act of Missouri'.

headings.title: Definitions for Route 66 signage program
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, subdivisions (1)–(9), and history note. Defines 'Alignment', 'Centennial celebration', 'Department', 'Historical roadside features', 'Right-of-way', 'Route 66', 'Signage program', 'Supplemental signage', and 'Theft-prevention mechanisms' for this section.

headings.title: Program establishment, scope, funding use, and sign standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Establishes the Route 66 Maintenance and Enhancement Program in MoDOT to maintain and repair existing supplemental signage, permits expansion onto county and city roads highlighting historical roadside features, governs use of subsection 7 moneys, and mandates compliance with MoDOT's Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices. Revised during review to avoid unexpanded acronym 'MUTCD' absent from the statutory text.

headings.title: Design guidelines, local collaboration, deadlines, and ongoing maintenance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Sets January 31, 2026 deadline for design uniformity guidelines with the section 620.2200 centennial commission, mandates county/municipal collaboration, sets May 30, 2026 completion deadline for sign replacement and new installation, and requires ongoing regular-program monitoring and maintenance.

headings.title: Theft-prevention measures for Route 66 signs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires the program to include theft-prevention measures including anti-theft hardware and discreet 'REPRODUCTION' markings.

headings.title: Route 66 Association of Missouri guidance and assistance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Directs MoDOT to seek historical-context guidance, placement expertise, and assistance from the Route 66 Association of Missouri.

headings.title: Route 66 Supplemental Signage Fund creation and administration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7, subdivisions (1)–(3), and history note. Creates the dedicated Route 66 Supplemental Signage Fund with state treasurer custody and sections 30.170/30.180 disbursements (subdivision (1)), exempts balances from section 33.080 biennial reversion (subdivision (2)), and directs fund investment with interest credited to the fund (subdivision (3)).

headings.title: Optional matching grants for local governments and organizations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Authorizes (permissively, 'may') MoDOT to establish a matching grant program for local governments and organizations for local signage needs or enhancements. Revised during review to reflect permissive authority rather than implying a mandatory grant entitlement.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Directs MoDOT director rulemaking subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 and includes a nonseverability clause invalidating the grant and post-August 28, 2025 rules if legislative chapter 536 review powers are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Legislative findings on scenic roads and highways
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1207). States general assembly findings on preserving, protecting, and enhancing scenic and natural-area roads and improving intergovernmental coordination.

headings.title: Authority to establish state scenic byways system
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes the commission to create a state scenic byways system for vehicular, bicycle, and pedestrian travel and to establish protective standards for design, access, maintenance, preservation, and identification.

headings.title: Local application and approval for scenic byway designation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits county commissions or municipal governing bodies to apply for scenic byway designation after a public hearing with >=30-day notice, requiring commission approval unless the road fails commission standards.

headings.title: Local application and conditions for removing scenic byways
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Permits county commissions or municipal governing bodies to apply for removal after a >=30-day noticed public hearing, directing commission approval unless opposed by a majority of residents along the byway or if the road fails commission standards.

headings.title: Designation or removal of joint-jurisdiction roads
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Prohibits commission designation or withdrawal of joint-jurisdiction roads until all affected municipal governing bodies and county commissions approve after >=30-day noticed public hearings.

headings.title: Preservation of local jurisdiction over scenic byways
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Preserves county commission, municipal, and county authority over scenic byways equal to their authority over other roads under their jurisdiction.

headings.title: Minimum factors for scenic byway designation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(5), and history note (L. 1995 S.B. 212 § 226.799 subsecs. 1, 2). Lists five minimum factors the commission must consider when designating a scenic byway: natural-beauty design, scenic/natural/historical/cultural/recreational resources, adequate safe-enjoyment land area, management compatibility, and nearby protected public areas.

headings.title: Rating system for scenic byway designation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the commission to adopt a rating system ensuring only roads displaying outstanding subsection 1 characteristics are designated under section 226.797.

headings.title: Marking national historic trails and Santa Fe Trail origins
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1986 H.B. 907 § 1). Directs MoDOT to mark primary routes of national historic trails (including seven listed trails) with NPS-approved signs on and crossing public highways once NPS plans are published and distributed, plus signs recognizing Franklin and Arrow Rock when marking the Santa Fe Trail.

headings.title: Acceptance of donations for historic trail signs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes (permissively) the commission to accept and administer gifts and donations to aid in obtaining approved historic trail signs.

headings.title: Outdoor advertising rules and commercial-industrial zoning exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1995 S.B. 212 § 226.799 subsecs. 4, 5). Authorizes commission rules regulating or prohibiting outdoor advertising visible from section 226.797 scenic byways (on-premise signs may be regulated but not prohibited) and bars commercial or industrial zoned areas from scenic byway designation.

headings.title: Tourist-oriented directional signs on scenic byways
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes commission rules for right-of-way tourist-oriented directional signs for businesses, services, natural attractions, and activities serving primarily non-local seasonal motorists, restricted exclusively to section 226.797 scenic byways.

headings.title: Committee creation and agency membership
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1988 S.B. 676 § 1 through A.L. 2018 S.B. 975 & 1024 Revision). Creates the 'Interagency Committee on Special Transportation' within MoDOT (noting official catchline discrepancy reading 'Interstate agency committee') and names member agency officials/designees plus governor-added executive-order representatives.

headings.title: Joint and individual committee planning and funding duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, subdivisions (1)–(9), and history note. Enumerates joint and individual duties for substate special transportation areas, planning councils (staffed by regional planning commissions with MoDOT funds), uniform planning/budgeting/reporting standards and agency rules, annual allocations, five-year planning budgets, substate fund-division rules (preserving source phrasing 'develop administrative and adopt rules' in (7)), annual plan review, and expenditure conformity review (preserving 'areas' in (9)).

headings.title: Assistant for transportation as committee chairman
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Designates the assistant for transportation of MoDOT to serve as chairman of the committee. Revised during review to use the exact statutory title rather than generic 'Department assistant'.

headings.title: Department staffing for committee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs MoDOT to provide staff for the committee.

headings.title: Meeting schedule and fiscal-year expenditure scope
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs the committee to meet and perform duties to discharge responsibilities over special transportation expenditures for the state fiscal year beginning July 1, 1989 and subsequent years.

headings.title: Contingent termination upon certification of ten percent goal

headings.title: Creation, funding, nonlapse, and uses of recipients fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2021 S.B. 258 § 1; footnote notes 'monies' appears in original rolls for 'moneys*'). headings.title: Filing certified corridor map with authorities and recorders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1995 S.B. 212 § 226.952 subsecs. 1, 2). Authorizes (permissively) the commission, after approving a new or relocated state highway corridor location, to file a certified corridor map with each regulatory authority having jurisdiction and with the county recorder of deeds.

headings.title: Public hearing, agency consultation, and owner notice prerequisites
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Prohibits filing or recording a corridor map without first advertising and holding a public hearing, consulting jurisdictional regulatory authorities, cooperating with any 23 U.S.C. 134 metropolitan planning organization, and sending certified-mail notice to record parcel owners at least 30 days before the hearing.

headings.title: Exception for areas without a regulatory authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1995 S.B. 212 § 226.952 subsecs. 4 to 7). Renders sections 226.952–226.957 inapplicable and bars corridor map filing or recording in areas of the state having no regulatory authority.

headings.title: Exception for projects funded solely with state funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Renders sections 226.952–226.957 inapplicable and bars corridor map filing or recording for new or relocated state highway projects funded with state funds and no federal funds.

headings.title: Filing fee paid to regulatory authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the commission to pay a $250 filing fee to a regulatory authority upon filing a corridor map or revised corridor map to compensate for activities under sections 226.950–226.973.

headings.title: Exception for areas developed near maximum use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Renders sections 226.952–226.957 inapplicable and bars corridor map filing or recording for new or relocated state highways in areas already developed at or near maximum commercial, industrial, or residential use.

headings.title: Forty-five-day waiting period for local approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1995 S.B. 212 § 226.954 subsecs. 2 to 4). Prohibits a city or county regulatory authority from approving sections 226.959–226.967 applications or requests for corridor-abutting or corridor-interior property without commission concurrence until 45 days after commission receipt, unless earlier concurrence notice is received.

headings.title: Commission response options within forty-five-day period
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Lists commission written-notice options within the 45-day period to the regulatory authority and property owner: concur, recommend modifications or limits as approval conditions, or give notice of probable intent to acquire corridor property.

headings.title: Local authority to act after commission concurrence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Provides that upon commission concurrence in an application or request, the regulatory authority is free to act on it as provided by law.

headings.title: Bar on recording plats without full corridor compliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1995 S.B. 212 § 226.956). Prohibits any recorder of deeds from recording a subdivision or real property development plat when the property owner, a regulatory authority, or both have not fully complied with sections 226.950–226.973.

headings.title: Permits, plats, and zoning barred pending commission action
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Prohibits regulatory authorities from issuing specified commercial, industrial, or residential building permits, approving plats, or granting zoning, rezoning, variances, or exceptions within a properly filed and recorded corridor map until the commission has had required time to act and, if appropriate, acquire or begin condemnation.

headings.title: Commission enforcement actions and property restoration upon acquisition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1995 S.B. 212 § 226.958). Authorizes commission circuit court actions to prevent or undo violations of sections 226.950–226.973 and stop violating construction, and requires a court order restoring property to its pre-construction condition at owner expense if the commission acquires property developed in violation.

headings.title: Voidness of violating local or recorder actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Declares void and unenforceable any action taken by a regulatory authority or recorder of deeds in violation of sections 226.950–226.973.

headings.title: Preservation of local planning, zoning, and corridor enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1995 S.B. 212 § 226.960). Construes sections 226.950–226.973 not to limit regulatory authorities from incorporating corridors into master plans or zoning, adjusting setback lines, or taking lawful jurisdictional actions to preserve, protect, and enforce the corridor.

headings.title: Preservation of commission purchase and condemnation authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Construes sections 226.950–226.973 not to limit or restrict the commission's general authority to purchase or condemn fee simple or lesser interests in real property for right-of-way or other authorized purposes.
